index.title: Home
index.intro.heading: QuestCodex
index.intro.p1: A browser-based quest wiki for **the quests actually loaded on your own SPT server**.
index.intro.p2: External wiki sites track live EFT, which is not what your server runs. QuestCodex reads the quest tables your server holds in memory and builds the catalog from those. If a quest mod changed a condition or a reward, you see the changed value, and quests a mod added show up in the same list as the vanilla ones, tagged with the mod they came from.
index.intro.p3: It only **reads** server data. It never modifies quests, profiles or traders.
index.whats-inside.heading: What's inside
index.whats-inside.table1.r3c2: Every quest on your server, with filters, chains, rewards and mod attribution
index.whats-inside.table1.r4c2: What to bring before a raid: maps, weapons, gear, items to hand over or plant
index.whats-inside.table1.r5c2: Your profile's quest progress, raid prep per map, the items you still need, the quests that unlock items and your way to Kappa

getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.requirements.heading: Requirements
getting-started.requirements.li2: **No client plugin.** This is a server mod only, no BepInEx involved.
getting-started.installation.heading: Installation
getting-started.installation.li2: Extract it and overwrite the resulting `SPT_Runtime` folder into your SPT install root (e.g. `C:\SPT`, the parent folder of the `SPT_Runtime` folder containing `SPT.Server.exe`).
getting-started.installation.p1: If your server root is the `SPT_Runtime` folder itself (older SPT layout), copy just the `SPT_Runtime\user\mods\QuestCodex` folder from the zip into your server root's `user\mods\`.
getting-started.opening-it.heading: Opening it
getting-started.opening-it.p1: Start the server, then open **`https://127.0.0.1:6969/questcodex`** in your browser. You can also reach it from the mod card on the SPT server web page (`https://127.0.0.1:6969`).
getting-started.opening-it.li1: If you get a certificate warning, proceed. It's the same self-signed certificate the SPT server web page uses.
getting-started.opening-it.li2: The SPT server binds to `127.0.0.1` only, so the page opens **only in a browser on the machine running the server**. Phones and other PCs cannot reach it.
getting-started.opening-it.li3: You can keep it open on a second monitor while playing. It's read-only and doesn't touch the game.
getting-started.language-and-theme.heading: Language and theme
getting-started.language-and-theme.li1: **Language**: `English` / `한국어` / `Русский`. UI strings and quest/item names change together (game text comes from the server's locale tables).
getting-started.language-and-theme.img.topbar-switches: Refresh data, theme and language switches
getting-started.refresh-data.heading: Refresh data
getting-started.refresh-data.p1: Map and loot data are built once per server run and kept on disk, so later starts are fast. If you change mod settings that affect loot (such as a loot preset) without changing the mod list, press **Refresh data** at the right of the top bar to rebuild it. It takes about 10 seconds.
getting-started.side-menu.heading: Side menu
getting-started.side-menu.p1: The menu button at the left of the top bar hides or shows the side menu, and the choice is remembered.

wiki/index.title: Wiki
wiki/index.intro.p1: Every quest loaded on your server in one list, vanilla and mod quests alike.

wiki/quest-list.title: Quest list
wiki/quest-list.trader-filter.heading: Trader filter
wiki/quest-list.trader-filter.p1: Pick a trader from the avatar row to see only their quests. Mod-added traders are listed too.
wiki/quest-list.search-and-filter-chips.heading: Search and filter chips
wiki/quest-list.search-and-filter-chips.p1: Search by quest name, and narrow the list with the `Vanilla` / `Mod` and `BEAR only` / `USEC only` chips.
wiki/quest-list.mod-filter.heading: Mod filter
wiki/quest-list.mod-filter.p1: When your server has mod quests and the `Mod` chip is on, a **Source mod** row appears under the filter bar. Mods often add quests to vanilla traders, so this is the quickest way to see everything one mod added.
wiki/quest-list.mod-filter.li1: Pick one or more mods. **All mods** clears the selection
wiki/quest-list.mod-filter.li2: It combines with the trader filter, and the trader row recounts for the selected mods
wiki/quest-list.mod-filter.li3: Chip dots use the same colors as the mod tags in the list
wiki/quest-list.vanilla-quests-a-mod-overrides.heading: Vanilla quests a mod overrides
wiki/quest-list.vanilla-quests-a-mod-overrides.p1: Some quest mods replace the files of vanilla quests instead of adding new ones. Those quests stay vanilla, but they carry the mod's name in a tag with a dashed outline, in the wiki and on the progress pages.
wiki/quest-list.vanilla-quests-a-mod-overrides.li1: The mod gets its own chip in the **Source mod** row, with a hollow dot, so you can list every quest it overrides
wiki/quest-list.vanilla-quests-a-mod-overrides.li2: The expanded quest's meta line reads **Vanilla quest overridden by a mod**
wiki/quest-list.sorting.heading: Sorting
wiki/quest-list.sorting.li1: **By chain** (default): prerequisites always sit above the quests they unlock
wiki/quest-list.compact-tags.heading: Compact tags
wiki/quest-list.compact-tags.p1: The **Compact tags** button left of the sort menu shrinks each mod name tag into a colored dot, so long mod names don't crowd the quest names.
wiki/quest-list.compact-tags.li1: Dots use the same colors as the **Source mod** chips; overridden vanilla quests get a hollow dot
wiki/quest-list.compact-tags.li2: Hover a dot to see the mod name
wiki/quest-list.compact-tags.li3: The wiki and the progress quest list each remember their own setting
wiki/quest-list.deep-links.heading: Deep links
wiki/quest-list.deep-links.p1: `?quest=<questId>` opens a specific quest directly, so you can bookmark or share a quest.

wiki/quest-details.title: Quest details
wiki/quest-details.inline-expansion.heading: Inline expansion
wiki/quest-details.inline-expansion.p1: Click a quest row and it expands in place with objectives, requirements, rewards (including on-accept and on-fail rewards) and its prerequisite and unlock links. Several rows can stay open at once.
wiki/quest-details.chain-jumps.heading: Chain jumps
wiki/quest-details.chain-jumps.p1: Click a prerequisite or unlocked quest name in the expanded row to jump straight to it.
wiki/quest-details.description-popup.heading: Description popup
wiki/quest-details.description-popup.p1: The full quest description opens in a popup, so long text doesn't stretch the list.
wiki/quest-details.quest-locations-map.heading: Quest locations map
wiki/quest-details.quest-locations-map.p1: The **Locations** button next to the guide button opens a map of where the quest's objectives are. It's greyed out when no objective has location data.
wiki/quest-details.quest-locations-map.li1: Each objective gets a numbered marker; kill-zone and flare objectives are drawn as areas, one color per objective
wiki/quest-details.quest-locations-map.li2: Map tabs switch maps, and floor buttons switch floors. A red dot on a floor button means that floor has objectives too
wiki/quest-details.quest-locations-map.li3: Wheel to zoom, drag to pan, double-click to fit
wiki/quest-details.quest-locations-map.li4: **Locked doors** shows lock icons for locked doors and keycard doors. Hover one to see the key it needs
wiki/quest-details.quest-locations-map.li5: **Extracts** shows extracts and transits as shield icons, colored for PMC, shared and scav extracts. Hover one to see its name and side, plus its requirement (e.g. a fee or climbing gear) and spawn chance when it has them. Extracts on other floors are drawn dimmed
wiki/quest-details.quest-locations-map.p2: QuestCodex doesn't know which quests need a key, but the map gets you most of the way: if a marker sits next to a lock icon, hover it to see which key opens that door, and you can judge for yourself whether to bring it.
wiki/quest-details.icebreaker.heading: Icebreaker
wiki/quest-details.icebreaker.p1: The Icebreaker map is ready ahead of SPT v5. Until then, it shows up as soon as your server has the Icebreaker location, for example from a mod that adds it.
wiki/quest-details.icebreaker.li1: Floors are the ship's decks (`Deck -3` to `Deck 10`)
wiki/quest-details.icebreaker.li2: Besides key and keycard doors, the door tooltip covers keypad doors (with the code when it's fixed), doors you blow open with an explosive charge and frozen hatches you melt with a gas torch
wiki/quest-details.icebreaker.li3: Repair objectives that point at a switch, like the breaker panels in Wiring the Vessel, get markers too
wiki/quest-details.icebreaker.img.wiki-quest-map-icebreaker: Icebreaker map for Wiring the Vessel
wiki/quest-details.expanded-interchange.heading: Expanded Interchange
wiki/quest-details.expanded-interchange.p1: If a mod that expands Interchange is loaded, the map and its quest zones, areas and locked doors switch to the expanded version, and the tab reads **Interchange (Expanded)**. Without it, nothing changes.
wiki/quest-details.branch-warnings.heading: Branch warnings
wiki/quest-details.branch-warnings.p1: Some quests sit on mutually exclusive branches: finishing one fails or locks the other. These quests carry a branch tag in the list, and the details warn you which quests you would lock out.
wiki/quest-details.mod-attribution.heading: Mod attribution
wiki/quest-details.mod-attribution.p1: Quests from mods carry their source mod's name, color-coded per mod.
wiki/quest-details.mod-attribution.img.wiki-mod-list: Mod quests with their source mod tags
wiki/quest-details.mod-attribution.p2: Quests a mod injects from C# code rather than from JSON files leave no file trace, so their source mod can't be identified. Those get a generic `mod` label instead.

wiki/quest-guide.title: Quest guide
wiki/quest-guide.intro.p1: Hit the **Guide** button on a quest to see what to bring before a raid.
wiki/quest-guide.what-it-shows.heading: What it shows
wiki/quest-guide.what-it-shows.li1: The map the quest takes place on
wiki/quest-guide.what-it-shows.li4: Items to hand over or plant, with found-in-raid requirements
wiki/quest-guide.what-it-shows.li5: Rules like finishing in a single raid or using specific exits
wiki/quest-guide.what-it-shows.p2: Long lists collapse to the first few entries. Click **+N more** to see them all.
wiki/quest-guide.moving-and-resizing.heading: Moving and resizing
wiki/quest-guide.moving-and-resizing.li1: Drag the header to move the popup.
wiki/quest-guide.moving-and-resizing.li2: Drag any edge to resize it.
wiki/quest-guide.moving-and-resizing.li3: Your layout is remembered. Double-click the header to reset it.

progress/index.title: Progress
progress/index.intro.p1: The Progress menu shows where a profile stands and what it still needs. It has five pages:
progress/index.intro.table1.r3c2: Trader progress, quests you can act on now, quests by status
progress/index.intro.table1.r4c2: Everything to do on the map you're about to play
progress/index.intro.table1.r5c2: Items your remaining quests still ask for, against what you have
progress/index.intro.table1.r6c2: Quests left before an item is sold by a trader or can be crafted
progress/index.intro.table1.r7c2: What's left before the Kappa container, as a list or a tree per trader
progress/index.choosing-a-profile.heading: Choosing a profile
progress/index.choosing-a-profile.p1: The profile bar at the top is shared by all five pages. It starts on the profile that is currently online and remembers your choice in the browser.
progress/index.live-updates.heading: Live updates
progress/index.live-updates.p1: The pages refresh on their own when the game saves your profile (for example after a raid or a turn-in) and when you come back to the tab. Quests that changed are briefly highlighted.

progress/overview.title: Overview
progress/overview.trader-progress.heading: Trader progress
progress/overview.trader-progress.p1: A progress bar per trader with finished and total quest counts. Traders you've fully finished turn green.
progress/overview.what-you-can-do-now.heading: What you can do now
progress/overview.what-you-can-do-now.li1: **Ready to turn in**: every objective is done
progress/overview.what-you-can-do-now.li2: **Available to accept**: quests you can pick up now
progress/overview.what-you-can-do-now.li3: **Can hand over now**: hand-over objectives your items already cover
progress/overview.quests-by-status.heading: Quests by status
progress/overview.quests-by-status.p1: All quests grouped by status, with search and the same trader row as the wiki. Mod quests carry their mod name tag. The same [source mod filter](../wiki/quest-list.html#mod-filter) sits under the status tabs, and the tab counts and trader row follow the mods you pick.
progress/overview.quests-by-status.p2: Click a quest to expand the same details as the wiki (description, guide, locations map, branch warning, rewards, related quests), plus your progress:
progress/overview.quests-by-status.li1: Objectives show their counters, and finished ones are struck through
progress/overview.quests-by-status.li2: Locked quests mark the start conditions you haven't met yet, with your current value
progress/overview.quests-by-status.li3: **Open in wiki** jumps to the quest in the wiki; related quest links jump within this list
progress/overview.quests-by-status.li4: Each quest under **Unlocks** shows how many follow-ups it still has left
progress/overview.quests-by-status.p3: Each tab sorts for what you'd look for first:
progress/overview.quests-by-status.li5: **Active**: ready to turn in first, then by objective completion
progress/overview.quests-by-status.p4: Quests you can never finish on this profile (other faction only, or a branch you already closed) are marked **Unreachable**.
progress/overview.follow-ups-and-sorting.heading: Follow-ups and sorting
progress/overview.follow-ups-and-sorting.p1: Each row shows **N follow-ups**: how many quests that quest eventually leads to and you haven't finished yet. It follows unlocks all the way down and counts a shared branch only once. Quests at the end of a chain show nothing.
progress/overview.follow-ups-and-sorting.p2: The sort menu next to the search box picks the order:
progress/overview.follow-ups-and-sorting.li2: **Most follow-ups left**: quests that open up the most first

progress/raid-prep.title: Raid prep
progress/raid-prep.intro.p1: Pick the map you're about to play and see everything your active quests want there.
progress/raid-prep.map-tabs.heading: Map tabs
progress/raid-prep.map-tabs.p1: Each map tab shows how many open objectives it has. A map your server has gets a tab even with no quests on it yet, such as the Icebreaker, so you can still check its extracts and locked doors.
progress/raid-prep.quests-on-this-map.heading: Quests on this map
progress/raid-prep.quests-on-this-map.p1: Quests with objectives on the selected map, plus objectives you can do on any map, grouped per quest. Expanding a quest dims the objectives that belong to other maps.
progress/raid-prep.quests-on-this-map.p2: Quests drawn on the map come first, then quests with counters by progress, then the rest by name.
progress/raid-prep.map.heading: Map
progress/raid-prep.map.p1: Under the quest lists sits a map card that follows the selected map tab and stays in view while you scroll. It's the same map as the wiki's [quest locations map](../wiki/quest-details.html#quest-locations-map), with all the quests on this map at once.
progress/raid-prep.map.li1: Quest rows carry the same colored number as their markers. Hover either side to highlight the other
progress/raid-prep.map.li2: Floor buttons, objective areas and the **Locked doors** toggle work like in the wiki. Lock icons near a marker tell you which key you may want to bring
progress/raid-prep.map.li3: **Extracts** shows the map's extracts and transits. Hover one to check its requirement and spawn chance before you plan your way out
progress/raid-prep.map.p2: **Expand** opens the map in a movable, resizable window with a numbered quest list. The page behind it stays scrollable and clickable. Close it with the close button or `Esc`.
progress/raid-prep.bring-with-you--items-to-loot.heading: Bring with you / Items to loot
progress/raid-prep.bring-with-you--items-to-loot.li1: **Bring with you**: items to plant on this map, with how many you need and how many you have
progress/raid-prep.bring-with-you--items-to-loot.li2: **Items to loot**: items your quests want you to find on this map
progress/raid-prep.bring-with-you--items-to-loot.img.progre: Bring with you and items to loot
progress/raid-prep.gear-and-special-conditions.heading: Gear and special conditions
progress/raid-prep.gear-and-special-conditions.li1: **Gear · Weapons**: required or banned gear and allowed weapons, grouped per quest
progress/raid-prep.gear-and-special-conditions.li2: **Special conditions**: rules like completing in a single raid or using a specific exit
progress/raid-prep.gear-and-special-conditions.p1: Objectives without map data take the map named in their text, and are marked as inferred.

progress/needed-items.title: Needed items
progress/needed-items.intro.p1: Everything your remaining quests still ask you to hand over or plant, compared with what you have.
progress/needed-items.the-table.heading: The table
progress/needed-items.the-table.p1: Each row sums one item across all remaining quests, next to how many you hold in your stash and how many of those are found in raid. Expand a row to see which quests need it.
progress/needed-items.filters.heading: Filters
progress/needed-items.filters.li1: **Category**: the icon row above the table filters by item category (ammo, keys, electronics, ...)
progress/needed-items.filters.li3: **In stash (don't sell)**: items you already have and should keep
progress/needed-items.filters.li4: **FIR required**: items that must be found in raid
progress/needed-items.filters.p1: When a quest accepts any one of several items, they count as a single line. Quests you can't reach (other faction, a branch you've closed) are left out of the totals.
progress/needed-items.what-counts-as-in-stash.heading: What counts as "in stash"
progress/needed-items.what-counts-as-in-stash.p1: Your stash and the gear you're wearing, the same as the in-game hand-over window. Hideout stashes are not counted.

progress/unlock-paths.title: Unlock paths
progress/unlock-paths.intro.p1: Items that a quest unlocks for sale at a trader or as a craft, and the quests you still have to finish to get there.
progress/unlock-paths.the-list.heading: The list
progress/unlock-paths.the-list.p1: Each row is one item, sorted by how many quests are left before you can get it.
progress/unlock-paths.the-list.li1: **Closest source**: the trader sale or craft that takes the fewest quests, with `+N` when there are more
progress/unlock-paths.the-list.li2: **Do now**: the quest to work on next, or what's blocking it (a level or a quest status you need first)
progress/unlock-paths.the-list.p2: Use the chips (**All**, **Trader sale**, **Crafting**, **Unlocked**, **Unreachable**), the category icon row and the search box to narrow the list. Search ignores spaces.
progress/unlock-paths.the-list.p3: One-time quest rewards and items a trader sells at a loyalty level alone aren't listed. They don't need a quest path.
progress/unlock-paths.closest-path.heading: Closest path
progress/unlock-paths.closest-path.p1: Click a row to see the path for its closest source. The card lists the quests in order, from what you can do now to the goal quest, and long paths fold in the middle. The bottom line sums up the quests left, the highest level required on the way and any trader loyalty or standing the quests ask for.
progress/unlock-paths.closest-path.p2: When an item has several sources, the list on the right switches between them.
progress/unlock-paths.closest-path.img.progress-unlocks-detail: Expanded row with the closest path
progress/unlock-paths.full-path.heading: Full path
progress/unlock-paths.full-path.p1: **Full path ›** opens every quest on the path, step by step. Quests in the same step can be done in any order, and each step groups them by trader. Quests above your level and branch quests that would fail another quest are marked. Drag the window's edges to resize it.
progress/unlock-paths.focusing-on-one-quest.heading: Focusing on one quest
progress/unlock-paths.focusing-on-one-quest.p1: Some paths branch out a lot. Searching `kit` and opening **Weapon repair kit** on a level 47 profile, for example, gives 38 quests across many traders, which is hard to follow at once.
progress/unlock-paths.focusing-on-one-quest.p2: Click the quest you're on, such as **The Survivalist Path - Tough Guy**, and the window keeps only the quests connected to it: the quests it needs and the quests that need it, down to the goal. The result is one short route you can follow from start to end.
progress/unlock-paths.focusing-on-one-quest.li1: **+ N other prereq(s)** marks a quest that also needs quests from other branches, which are hidden while focusing
progress/unlock-paths.focusing-on-one-quest.li2: **Open in wiki** opens the focused quest in the wiki, and **Show all** goes back to the full path
progress/unlock-paths.unreachable-sources.heading: Unreachable sources
progress/unlock-paths.unreachable-sources.p1: A source is marked unreachable when its path goes through a quest you can no longer finish on this profile:
progress/unlock-paths.unreachable-sources.li2: The other side of an exclusive branch you already took
progress/unlock-paths.unreachable-sources.li3: A quest for the other faction only
progress/unlock-paths.unreachable-sources.li4: A quest the server keeps locked (events and the like)

progress/kappa-tracker.title: Kappa tracker
progress/kappa-tracker.intro.p1: What's left before the Collector quest and the Kappa container, and which Kappa quests to work on next.
progress/kappa-tracker.what-counts-toward-kappa.heading: What counts toward Kappa
progress/kappa-tracker.what-counts-toward-kappa.p1: The list isn't fixed. QuestCodex reads the Collector quest on your server and counts the quests it requires, plus every quest before them. Vanilla servers get the quest list as is, and quest mods that change the Collector requirements (for example by adding trader loyalty levels or a player level) are followed too.
progress/kappa-tracker.what-counts-toward-kappa.p2: Failed quests count as done when every later quest also accepts the failure, as with branch choices.
progress/kappa-tracker.summary.heading: Summary
progress/kappa-tracker.summary.li1: The left card has one bar per kind of requirement: **Kappa quests**, **Collector items (FIR)**, and **Level** or **Trader levels** when the Collector quest asks for them
progress/kappa-tracker.summary.li2: The right card shows Kappa quests done per trader. When the Collector quest asks for trader levels, a **Required** column shows them too
progress/kappa-tracker.quest-list.heading: Quest list
progress/kappa-tracker.quest-list.p1: The trader tabs above the list show how many Kappa quests each trader has left. Pick one to see only theirs.
progress/kappa-tracker.quest-list.li1: **Available**: quests you can accept or have in progress, longest remaining chain first. The right side names the Kappa quest that finishing this one unlocks, with `+N more` when there are several
progress/kappa-tracker.quest-list.li2: **Locked**: quests you can't take yet, the closest to opening first. Folded by default
progress/kappa-tracker.quest-list.li3: **Done**: finished Kappa quests, the latest first. Folded by default
progress/kappa-tracker.quest-list.p2: Click a row to see its objectives, requirements and rewards, the same detail as in the overview.
progress/kappa-tracker.quest-list.p3: A profile that has never entered the game has every quest locked. The list then explains why and names the quests that open first.
progress/kappa-tracker.quest-flow.heading: Quest flow
progress/kappa-tracker.quest-flow.p1: **Show full chain** opens the Kappa quests before and after one quest. The quest you picked is in the middle with a star, the Kappa quests you already finished above it are folded into one line, and the remaining ones follow step by step below. Long chains show the first steps with **Show N more steps**.
progress/kappa-tracker.quest-flow.p2: For **Gunsmith - Part 11**, for example, the 11 Kappa quests before it are folded as done, and the 11 parts left up to Part 22 follow below.
progress/kappa-tracker.quest-flow.p3: When a step has several quests, click the one you're on to keep only the quests connected to it, as in [Unlock paths](unlock-paths.html).
progress/kappa-tracker.tree-view.heading: Tree view
progress/kappa-tracker.tree-view.p1: Pick a trader tab and switch **List** to **Tree** to see that trader's Kappa quests as a tree. Each column is one step further down the prerequisites, and lines connect a quest to the quests it unlocks. The view you pick is remembered.
progress/kappa-tracker.tree-view.li1: Colors show **Completed**, **Available · In progress**, **Opens next** (every prerequisite is done or in progress) and **Locked**. A dashed line marks a quest that opens even if the branch quest before it failed
progress/kappa-tracker.tree-view.li2: A quest from another trader that one of these needs is drawn as a faint dotted box, one step back
progress/kappa-tracker.tree-view.li3: **Collapse completed** folds the finished quests into one box
progress/kappa-tracker.tree-view.li4: Drag with the mouse to move around a large tree
progress/kappa-tracker.tree-view.p2: Click a quest to highlight the quests it needs and the quests that need it. Its detail opens under the tree, with **Show full chain** and **Open in wiki**.
progress/kappa-tracker.collector-items.heading: Collector items
progress/kappa-tracker.collector-items.p1: The items the Collector quest asks you to hand over, with where to find them.
progress/kappa-tracker.collector-items.li1: **Status**: **Handed over**, **Have (FIR)**, **not FIR** (you have one that isn't found in raid) or **Missing**
progress/kappa-tracker.collector-items.li2: **Container loot**: the containers the item most often spawns in, with the chance it's inside when you open one. Hover for the full list
progress/kappa-tracker.collector-items.li3: **Body loot**: the kinds of bots that can carry it
progress/kappa-tracker.collector-items.li4: **Not handed in** / **All** and the search box narrow the table

limitations.title: Known limitations
limitations.mods-that-hook-responses-at-runtime.head: Mods that hook responses at runtime
limitations.mods-that-hook-responses-at-runtime.p1: QuestCodex reads the **quest tables the server merged into memory** once it finished booting. Every mod that adds or edits quest JSON is reflected exactly, regardless of load order.
limitations.mods-that-hook-responses-at-runtime.p2: A mod that intercepts a route like `/client/quest/list` and **rewrites the response on each request** never touches those tables, so its changes don't reach QuestCodex. You'd see the modified quest in game and the unmodified one here.
limitations.mods-that-hook-responses-at-runtime.p3: If the page and the game disagree, suspect this first.
limitations.mod-quests-added-from-c-code.heading: Mod quests added from C# code
limitations.mod-quests-added-from-c-code.p1: Quests a mod injects from C# code (`CustomQuestService.CreateQuest()`) rather than from JSON files leave no file trace, so their source mod can't be identified. Those get a generic `mod` label.
limitations.quest-map-coverage.heading: Quest map coverage
limitations.quest-map-coverage.li1: A few quests have no location data, so their objectives don't appear on the map.
limitations.quest-map-coverage.li2: Mod quests show on the map only when the mod defines its zones in data the server can read, or when QuestCodex already ships their positions (the Icebreaker quests do).
limitations.quest-map-coverage.li3: Maps a mod adds are drawn only when QuestCodex ships a map for them (currently the Icebreaker and the expanded Interchange).
limitations.quest-map-coverage.li4: Extract and transit positions come from bundled data, so an extract a mod adds or moves may be missing or misplaced.
limitations.quest-map-coverage.li5: QuestCodex doesn't track which keys you own. Lock icons tell you which key a door needs, nothing more.
limitations.unlock-paths.heading: Unlock paths
limitations.unlock-paths.p1: The path summary checks the required level against your profile, but trader loyalty and standing are only listed, not checked. **Quests left** counts quests only.
limitations.overridden-vanilla-quests.heading: Overridden vanilla quests
limitations.overridden-vanilla-quests.p1: A vanilla quest is marked as overridden when a mod ships a file that replaces it. QuestCodex doesn't check whether the mod actually changed anything in it.
limitations.kappa-tracker.heading: Kappa tracker
limitations.kappa-tracker.li1: Container chances for Collector items are worked out from your server's loot tables and averaged over the maps, so they're estimates, not drop rates you'll see in every raid.
limitations.kappa-tracker.li2: Only the Collector hand-in items get loot sources.
limitations.local-only.heading: Local only
limitations.local-only.p1: The SPT server binds to `127.0.0.1`, so QuestCodex opens only in a browser on the machine running the server.
